marks.gloss_en: הא נחה -- חייב? והלא נזכר, ותנן: כל חייבי חטאות אינן חייבין עד שתהא תחלתן וסופן שגגה -- he remembered before it landed, so its end was not unwitting
[by implication:] if it came to rest -- he is liable
תרתי קתני: liability on landing belongs to the case where he did not remember (= p_rava_tarti)
והא 'זה הכלל' דקתני -- אזריקה קתני: the principle is taught of throwing, not of carrying
Rava: it teaches two [cases]: one who throws and remembered after it left his hand; or else, did not remember, and another caught it, a dog caught it, or it was burnt -- exempt
חסורי מחסרא: liability on landing is where he forgot again (= p_rav_ashi_chasurei, p_rav_ashi_chazar_veshachach)

Rav Ashi: [the mishna] is lacking, and teaches thus: one who throws and remembered after it left his hand -- another caught it, a dog caught it, or it was burnt -- exempt; if it came to rest -- liable

לכתא ומתנא -- אוגדו בידו הוא! a bolt on a cord is held in his hand [so it is no throw]. (The stam's defence, כגון שנתכוין לעשות חבורה, is p_lachta_chabura, itself felled by obj_tneina_chabura; the sugya then turns away with אלא.)
הא נמי תנינא: הזורק לעשות חבורה ... ונזכר עד שלא נעשית חבורה -- פטור -- the wounding case is already taught in the mishna
[the bolt and cord is] where he intended to make a wound
one who throws, and remembered after it left his hand -- another caught it, a dog caught it, or it was burnt -- exempt
אף אנן נמי תנינא: R' Meir obligates one who carried food out in his mouth, though that is not the way of carrying (ואמאי? הא אין דרך הוצאה בכך) -- so his intent makes it a place
the mishna: one may eat one eating and be liable for four sin-offerings and one guilt-offering -- an impure man who ate forbidden fat that was notar of consecrated offerings, on Yom Kippur
הכא נמי, כיון דקא מיכוין -- מחשבתו משויא ליה מקום: as the mouth, so the dog's mouth
R' Meir: also, if it was Shabbat and he carried it out in his mouth -- liable
והאנן תנן: קלטה אחר או קלטה הכלב או שנשרפה -- פטור! -- the mishna exempts when a dog caught it
התם דלא מכוין, הכא דקא מכוין -- there he did not intend, here he intends (= p_hatam_dela_mechaven)
Rabba: one who threw and it came to rest in a dog's mouth or in the mouth of a furnace -- liable
Rabba: two cubits unwitting, two intentional, two unwitting -- exempt
in what case? if throwing -- it is unwitting [throughout]! rather, in carrying
Rava: two cubits unwitting, two intentional, two unwitting -- liable
[the mishna:] this is the principle: all who are liable to sin-offerings [are liable only if their beginning and end are unwitting]
